channel.title: Frontier Wire
channel.description: AI news: frontier labs, research, policy and commentary.

item.title: Dunzo cofounder Kabeer Biswas' AI startup M raises $9 Mn
item.description: Dunzo cofounder Kabeer Biswas' AI startup M has raised $9 million in a funding round led by RTP Global. This brings the startup's total capital raised to about $20 million following a previous $11 million seed round. The funding shows venture capital backing continuing for consumer tech attempts at AI-powered household management in Bengaluru.

item.title: Developers propose vertical data centers as Kansas City blocks high-rise plan
item.description: Developers are proposing vertical data centers to address high demand and land limits in places like Taiwan. However, Kansas City recently rejected a 20-story tower proposal. While AI infrastructure demand remains high, community resistance to building high-rise facilities threatens to slow down urban data center expansion.

item.title: Delhi High Court to examine if AI can be author under copyright law
item.description: The Delhi High Court issued notice on an appeal by American computer scientist Stephen L Thaler challenging the Copyright Office's refusal to recognise his AI system DABUS as the author of an artwork. The Copyright Office previously ruled that while the artwork met originality requirements, an AI system cannot be an author under Section 2(d)(vi) of the Copyright Act, 1957. This case addresses a fundamental legal distinction between whether an AI tool can hold authorship status or whether creators who design and train systems retain all ownership rights.

item.title: China humanoid robot investment to rise, selective use by 2027
item.description: Investment in humanoid robots in China is projected to accelerate, with selective commercial use anticipated in 2027 according to a Morgan Stanley report. The report highlights that spending on data collection, robot training, and early customer deployments is likely to increase. Component suppliers could benefit from rising hardware orders even before humanoid robots see widespread commercial adoption.

item.title: UK regulator warns AI agents must provide user control as Meta Muse launches
item.description: The UK Competition and Markets Authority warned that businesses offering personal AI agents must give consumers control over data access and agent autonomy. The guidance follows Meta's launch of its personal AI agent, Muse, in the UK. UK regulators are actively setting compliance boundaries for autonomous AI tools as Big Tech products enter the market.

item.title: Los Angeles school district blocks AI search features on student devices
item.description: Los Angeles Unified School District has temporarily disabled AI-generated search summaries on school-issued devices amid growing friction between school districts and Google over bundled artificial intelligence tools. The half-million-student district made the change without a formal public announcement following concerns from parent and activist groups. While school districts previously announced temporary moratoriums on generative AI use, this action represents a technical workaround implemented by a major district against a dominant technology provider that has stated it will not separate search products from education AI tools.

item.title: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman holds first Gen Z pre-budget meeting
item.description: Indian Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman held her first dedicated pre-Budget consultation with 22 Gen Z representatives on November 26, 2026, focusing on artificial intelligence, jobs, and skill development. The meeting marked the 13th and final session in the Finance Ministry's pre-Budget consultation series for the Union Budget 2027-28. By bringing youth representatives into traditional economic planning, the government is formally incorporating demands for emerging technologies and skill alignment directly into national fiscal discussions.

item.title: Japan's JERA enters talks with Anthropic and Meta to build data centres
item.description: Japan's largest power generator, JERA, is in talks with Anthropic and Meta to build data centres near power plants around Tokyo. The discussions form part of JERA's broader infrastructure push, which includes a planned $15 billion hyperscale data centre in Chiba. The discussions illustrate how major energy suppliers are coordinating directly with artificial intelligence developers to secure dedicated power sources for heavy computing demands.

item.title: Bharti Airtel to invest ₹1,200 crore in three Assam data centres
item.description: Bharti Airtel has signed an MoU with the Assam government to invest ₹1,200 crore in three data centres across Guwahati, Jorhat, and Silchar. The facilities will have a combined capacity of 40 MW and are expected to be completed by 2028. The project extends high-capacity digital infrastructure beyond major metropolitan hubs into northeastern India, supporting regional growth in cloud computing and artificial intelligence.

item.title: Dante Security raises $10M seed to monitor enterprise AI agents
item.description: Dante Security has launched out of stealth with $10M in seed funding led by NFX to provide a platform for monitoring autonomous AI agents within organizations. The platform discovers agents, traces their actions, and assigns a named human owner to each agent. As organizations deploy autonomous AI agents that act using employee credentials, security teams face blind spots because existing tools treat agent actions as approved human activity.

item.title: Ethan Mollick on AI's potential to solve wicked problems
item.description: Ethan Mollick posted on Bluesky that AI can cheaply deliver personalized human-level help in any language to cellphone users. He argued that this makes complex problems in education, healthcare, and development potentially tractable. This perspective highlights a perceived gap between the technical capability of AI tools to address systemic global challenges and the current level of ambition applied to solving them.

item.title: AI could displace 24 million knowledge-worker jobs in five years: JP Morgan
item.description: A JP Morgan Wealth Management report estimates that AI could displace around 24 million knowledge-worker jobs globally over five years. The report notes that much of the adjustment may happen through leaving roles unfilled rather than through layoffs. The report estimates that US impacts could approach the rate of job losses seen during the Great Recession, though spread over five years instead of two.

item.title: Bipartisan congressional efforts to regulate AI face legislative obstacles
item.description: Bipartisan efforts in Congress to regulate artificial intelligence are gaining momentum. However, these initiatives face obstacles due to the slow pace of legislative work and turf battles between members of both parties. For professionals tracking AI policy, jurisdictional disputes in Congress highlight the structural hurdles facing federal oversight of technology.

item.title: Swiggy Instamart lays off 340 employees amid AI push and inventory shift
item.description: Swiggy's quick-commerce division, Instamart, is laying off 340 employees while restructuring its business amid increased AI adoption and a shift to an inventory model. The cutbacks come as the company faces competition from rivals including Zomato's Blinkit and Zepto. The restructuring illustrates how intense competition and automation pressures in the fast-delivery sector are directly impacting employment levels.

item.title: Florida man sentenced to 47 months in prison for AI voice crypto scam
item.description: A US judge sentenced David Anthony Sanchez to 47 months in prison for using artificial intelligence to impersonate Kick streamer N3on in a cryptocurrency fraud scheme. The scheme defrauded memecoin organizers of approximately $260,000 through fake accounts and AI-generated voice recordings. The case marks a concrete federal prison sentence for financial crimes executed via generative audio cloning, highlighting how courts are penalizing the misuse of synthetic voice technology.

item.title: SAP prepares plan to eliminate at least 10,000 positions for AI shift
item.description: SAP is preparing a plan to eliminate at least 10,000 positions, or 9% of its global staff. The restructuring aims to transform its software business for the artificial intelligence era. The restructuring highlights how major enterprise software providers are shifting capital and human resources away from traditional operations to prioritize artificial intelligence.

item.title: Avicena raises $100M+ Series C for microLED optical interconnects
item.description: Avicena raised over $100 million in a Series C funding round led by Intervest to commercialize its microLED-based optical interconnect technology for AI infrastructure. The funding included participation from corporate venture arms such as SK Hynix, Samsung, and AMD. As copper links and traditional lasers face physical limits in AI data centers, chipmakers are investing in alternative optical technologies to overcome data bottlenecks between processors and memory.

item.title: Chariot AI unveils Chariot-1 LLM and speech models under IndiaAI Mission
item.description: Chariot AI has launched the Chariot-1 model suite under the IndiaAI Mission, featuring an 11-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts language model and a text-to-speech system supporting 10 Indian languages. The models were pre-trained from scratch in India and incorporate research innovations designed to improve computational efficiency and reduce token usage. The release highlights government-backed efforts to build sovereign foundation models tailored to Indian scripts, addressing the high token costs and inefficiencies that standard English-centric models face in multilingual environments.

item.title: Texas resumes data center permitting and approves SpaceX gas plant
item.description: Texas resumed data center permitting by approving permits for SpaceX's $24 billion gas power plant. The approval occurred ahead of Democratic Governor Gina Hinojosa taking office in January. The rapid approval ahead of a change in political leadership highlights how companies are rushing to secure infrastructure permits before incoming administrations implement stricter oversight.

item.title: Netherlands seeks to block US MATCH Act restricting ASML China sales
item.description: The Dutch government announced it will resist the US proposed MATCH Act, which aims to restrict ASML Holding NV's sales and maintenance services in China. Dutch Foreign Minister Tom Berendsen stated that the Netherlands intends to prevent the bill from becoming law, calling the proposal a threat to Europe's most valuable company. The dispute pits a key American ally against US lawmakers attempting to include the export control measure in the fiscal year 2027 National Defense Authorization Act.

item.title: ASML CEO warns aggressive export controls will push China to build domestic tech
item.description: ASML CEO Christophe Fouquet argued that export controls should not completely cut off China, warning that such a strategy would backfire by accelerating domestic development. ASML holds a $520 billion de facto monopoly in making lithography machines for advanced AI chips. The debate highlights tensions between protecting advanced technology and maintaining market share, as ASML currently supplies China with equipment that is over a decade behind the cutting edge.

item.title: Z.ai misses GLM-5.5 launch as US rules and distillation curbs hit China AI
item.description: Z.ai missed the scheduled November release for its 3-trillion-parameter flagship model, GLM-5.5, due to US computing restrictions and anti-distillation measures. Rival Moonshot AI also warns that losing access to overseas computing power could double the interval between its major releases. These restrictions threaten the cost-advantage model that has allowed Chinese AI developers to compete globally despite ongoing hardware export controls.

item.title: Thariq Shihipar joins OpenAI after leaving Anthropic
item.description: Thariq Shihipar has joined OpenAI following his departure from Anthropic in October. Shihipar previously worked as a Member of Technical Staff on Anthropic's Claude Code team. The departure of a prominent public-facing engineer from Anthropic's Claude Code team to OpenAI illustrates the ongoing interchange of technical personnel between leading AI developers.

item.title: AI labs may hold unreleased breakthroughs that could break current cryptosystems
item.description: Computer scientist Scott Aaronson said leading AI labs likely possess major, unreleased algorithmic breakthroughs that could break deployed cryptosystems, though the exact nature of the breakthroughs is unknown. If the breakthroughs can undermine existing encryption, data security and financial systems that rely on current cryptography could be at risk.

item.title: Google mandates MCP server access for Workspace AI agents by February 2027
item.description: Google released Model Context Protocol servers for Workspace and mandated that AI agents use them instead of standard REST APIs starting February 1, 2027. The rules introduce dedicated agent identities, human approval for sensitive actions, and restrictions on training data. Developers building email assistants or coding agents on Google Workspace face a tight deadline to migrate architectures and handle restricted Gmail capabilities.

item.title: SoftBank default risk hits 4-year high amid AI investment worries
item.description: The cost of insuring SoftBank Group bonds against default rose to a four-year high as investors questioned whether its AI investments will become profitable fast enough to service its debts. SoftBank's five-year credit default swap spread widened by more than 20 basis points to 534.6 basis points, with its default probability at 34.8%. As a major investor in frontier model developer OpenAI, SoftBank is treated as a bellwether for the wider artificial intelligence sector, meaning market pressure on its bonds signals broader financial skepticism toward heavy AI infrastructure spending.

item.title: IndiaMART settles dispute with OpenAI over ChatGPT link exclusions
item.description: IndiaMART settled its legal dispute with OpenAI out of court after alleging that ChatGPT selectively excluded its website and seller listings from AI responses. The Calcutta High Court dismissed the appeal on November 17 following the settlement. The case highlights ongoing legal questions regarding whether AI search platforms can restrict third-party links based on foreign trade watchlists.

item.title: Memory chip shortages spark global procurement war rooms and 10x price hikes
item.description: Companies worldwide have created procurement war rooms as a global memory chip shortage pushes some chip prices up tenfold in a year, driving higher electronics prices. Memory chips power AI hardware, so shortages and price spikes could raise costs for AI training and inference deployments.

item.title: BharatGen launches Patram 1.5, a 7B vision-language model for documents
item.description: BharatGen has launched Patram 1.5, a 7.8-billion-parameter open-weight vision-language model designed to process complex, multilingual, and poor-quality documents as images. The model features prompt-controlled OCR and abstention capabilities, and is available on Hugging Face and the BharatGen Playground. Unlike traditional OCR pipelines that flatten visual cues by converting documents to text first, Patram 1.5 processes page images directly and flags unreadable fields for human review to reduce errors in regulated sectors like banking and healthcare.

item.title: Confidential data sent to Chinese AI startup MiniMax accessed by unknown parties
item.description: Confidential data submitted to Chinese AI startup MiniMax was accessed by unidentified parties, even after users asked that the data not be stored. The exposure was discovered by cybersecurity researcher HD Moore of Dragos, who traced private links to devices in Beijing, Shanghai and unusual activity from Russia’s Moscow region. The incident shows that data sent to foreign AI services can be exposed despite retention safeguards, raising security concerns for global users of Chinese models.
